name: Banh mi
summary: Banh mi is a light baguette with pâté, mayonnaise, pickles, herbs, and usually a protein. The bread should crackle. The filling should not be only meat.
origin: A colonial-era loaf adapted across the country. Hoi An’s versions are famous; every city has a morning stall. In Da Nang it is the breakfast you eat standing up, on the way to the beach or the Hoi An road.
howToEat: Eat it the morning it is baked. Point at the fillings if the stall has several.
A stall with a queue of office workers is a better sign than a picture menu in five languages.
where: In Hoi An, street stalls in the old town, the morning of the walk.

In Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam Tourism says the sandwich is said to have originated here. One page fills the baguette with pâté and chili sauce, then meats, fresh herbs, and pickled vegetables, usually carrot and daikon, and says the sauce ties salty, sweet, and spicy flavors. The local-eating page lists char siu, homemade pâté, soft butter, pickled papaya, and hot chili, and says some cooks add a sauce. The city itinerary says pickled vegetables and pork. The attractions page puts bánh mì at the end of the Ben Thanh hall. Visit HCMC names Bánh mì Hoa Mã on Bùi Viện. Bánh mì Huỳnh Hoa is at 26 Lê Thị Riêng. A shop figure on the local-eating page is not the city price.
priceBand: One of the cheapest full meals in the country.
seoDescription: What goes in a banh mi, and how to pick a stall.
